methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $380M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
ZeroAvia, a Series C-stage transportation company that has raised $380M+, operates in a sector with eight private peer references but lacks a sufficiently dense comparable set at the same stage and valuation tier to support reliable peer-median valuation. While the transportation sector includes notable private companies such as Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and Harbinger, none yielded three or more datapoints meeting adjacent-stage and similar-tier filters.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology provides the primary quantitative anchor. Applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $380M raised proxy yields a midpoint valuation of $646M. This reflects the normalized funding-to-valuation step observable in comparable venture stages, absent sector-specific comps.

The triangulated valuation range is $549M (low) to $743M (median), centered at $646M. This range carries material sensitivity to two key uncertainties: (1) the appropriateness of the 1.7x stage multiplier in aerospace and hydrogen propulsion, which may differ from broader venture norms; and (2) the absence of same-stage, same-sector peers materially limits cross-validation. Any final valuation assessment should treat this range as indicative pending availability of tighter comparable transaction data or operating metrics specific to the hydrogen propulsion subsector.
